class.name: WeatherState
class.brief_description: One weather: wind, clouds and their look, mist, precipitation, lightning and the picture's exposure, which [WeatherDirector] blends toward.
class.description: See the comment at the top of modules/weather/weather_director.h. Every value is blended over a change of weather.

members.member: Height of the clouds' underside, in metres above sea level. It may lie below the peaks, which then stand in the cloud.
Share of the sky the clouds cover.
How much light a metre of cloud takes. Higher gives darker bases and more solid towers; lower, thinner and brighter clouds. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_density].
How much the detail noise eats into the clouds' edges: 0 smooth, rounded blobs, 2 frayed, wispy edges. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_erosion].
Light carried round inside the clouds. Lower gives greyer clouds with darker cores; higher, brighter and softer. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_multiscatter].
How far a cloud's top leans downwind, in metres per metre up. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_shear].
Multiplies the thickness [member cloud_type] gives (a few hundred metres for a layer, about a kilometre for fair cumulus, 8 km for a storm tower). [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_thickness_scale].
The clouds' kind: 0 a flat layer (stratus), about 0.6 fair-weather heaps (cumulus), 1 towering storm clouds with an anvil (cumulonimbus).
How much one cloud's kind differs from the next round [member cloud_type]. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_type_spread].
How unevenly the cover is spread over the sky: 0 the same everywhere, 1 clumps and clear gaps. [member AtmosphereEffect.cloud_variation].

The picture's exposure in this weather, in stops (EV); negative is darker. The engine does not use it: the game's camera reads it, so a grey day is seen as grey and a storm as dark, though the eye adapts to both.
How strong the gusts are against the wind's speed.
Share of the sky the high, thin layer covers.
The high layer's kind: 0 streaks (cirrus), 1 small puffs (altocumulus).
How often lightning strikes.
How thick the mist in the valley is.
Height the mist reaches, in metres above sea level.
Rain or snow: how hard it falls and how wet the ground gets. [member temperature] says which.
Degrees C on the valley floor: rain or snow, frost, and the snow and freezing lines.
How churned the wind is.
The direction the wind blows toward, in degrees from north (+X) toward east (+Z).
Wind speed 10 m above the ground, in m/s.
